title: SO-F-01 Identity and scopes model, version 1: subjects, keys, expiry and revocation; scope types from personal to organisation; every authenticated request resolves to a subject and a scope; personal and organisational scopes never mix
request: Build layer of the Scope One programme, adapted from the unsigned fold of 30 Oct 2026 (fold id SO-F-01) and validated against memev main at d1c65ef. Contracts marked with a dagger are signed in the owner's vault and are not visible in this repository; they are cited by id only. Implements the design records SO-2.02 (Permission-aware knowledge access: retrieval governed by identity, project membership, classification, policy and jurisdiction); SO-2.14 (Business deployment: multi-person project permissions and team administration) (contracts/scope-one/specs). The decision record cites this contract by id and keeps only the gaps this one does not cover. Builds on signed vault contracts: MEM-134†, MEM-145†, MEM-146†, SO-09-A†. Source in the fold: #222 section 13.5 (identity, role, membership, purpose at retrieval and action time) and #223 FEDERATION.md (node identity); D-PI-PREREQ (the identity page and threat-model row fold here). Settled decisions this contract follows (owner decision 31 Oct 2026, docs/scope-one/DECISIONS.md): topology is local-first and the cloud is only a relay and a backup; every supported provider stands on equal footing and no work or tier depends on one; crdt-merge is reached only through the provider boundary of src/engine/merge.mjs (docs/EXTENSION-POINTS.md) and this contract adds no merge engine to the core; tiers follow docs/PRICING.md (Free core, Personal for up to 3 computers with no per-computer add-on, higher tiers by contacting us) with no Personal trial; the git backup keeps running every few minutes (sync.interval_min). Memory authority: ADR 7 (memory and project-state authority) is proposed in PR #325 and is not decided here; this contract cites it and the local-first decision, and keeps one store under the vault with no second database. Provenance: adapted from the unsigned fold of 30 Oct 2026. Changes: (1) converted from the vault task format to the memev spec format (named tests run as red-green checks on the own test file of the contract; inline regular expression flags became the flags key; hygiene and decision verifiers became commands or doc checks). (2) removed fold-only fields and the owner-decision marker field, reworded the stop rule that named a patent, and made the text pass the leak scan. (3) AC04 extended the MEM-134 separation tests, but MEM-134 is in progress and not on main (src/engine/identity.mjs has no separation tests). The separation test is written standalone here, and MEM-134 is cited only. (4) Local-first check added: subjects and scopes resolve on the computer with no hosted identity call; a test replaces the network modules with throwing wrappers. (5) AC06 pattern needed the multiline flag; the fold used a ^ anchor with a single-line match. (6) Boundary with PG-09.1 WP09-01 (signed node and agent identity, delegation, revocation, admission): this contract owns the subject and scope model and the resolution at the request boundary; WP09-01 builds node admission on it and should cite it. (7) No role-by-action matrix is introduced (ADR 5 stays open).

requirements: docs/schemas/identity-v1.json defines subjects (person, agent, device, node, operator, service) with keys, expiry and revocation, the scope types
every store write and every authenticated MCP and HTTP request resolves to a subject and a scope
a token or binding issued for a personal scope cannot read or write an organisational scope and the reverse
the role bindings of MEM-145 and MEM-146 resolve to subjects of the model (an agent subject bound to a person subject) without a second identity store
subject and scope resolution works with every non-loopback network call made to throw

tasks.description: Identity today is per device and per credential (device and client tokens, src/engine/tokens.mjs, with read, write and admin scopes; the open routes of src/server/http.mjs stay open). Business needs persons, roles and scopes; federation needs node and operator identity; policy at retrieval and action time needs a subject on every authenticated request. Nothing beyond the execution plane can be built before this model exists. This contract defines it with a schema, a validator and the resolution at the request boundary, building on the role bindings of MEM-145 and MEM-146 and the separation rules of MEM-134 (src/engine/identity.mjs). Personal keeps working with today's tokens: a device or client token resolves to its owner subject and the personal scope. The principals of SO-09-A (user, lead, specialist, remote seat) are the subjects this model names; SO-09-A is coordinated, not a dependency. MEM-134 depends on MEM-119, MEM-122 and MEM-123, which are drafts outside the signed set; the fold lists them.

criteria.statement: docs/schemas/identity-v1.json defines subjects (person, agent, device, node, operator, service) with keys, expiry and revocation, the scope types personal, team, department, project, programme, portfolio, site and organisation, and membership records; a token's identity scope is a field of its own, distinct from the read, write and admin scopes of src/engine/tokens.mjs; the validator accepts the fixtures and refuses a subject without an owner or a scope without a type

stop_rules: Stop and post BLOCKED when a criterion cannot pass without weakening a test, skipping a test or relaxing an assertion.
Stop and ask when the work would name a client product, a person, a server or a seat in repository text; the client names live in docs/CLIENTS.md only.
Stop when the work would add a runtime dependency, a model call, a network call at install or start, a second store for project state, or any reporting that is not opt-in and off by default.
Stop when the work would move convergence logic into the core, vendor the engine, or add a merge engine beside the provider boundary of src/engine/merge.mjs.

Stop when the work would implement a federation, replication, trust, admission or computation feature beyond the specification, schema, validator and conformance test the contract names; the product keeps the planned label on it.
If any criterion fails after the fix: STOP, report the measured result, the failing check and file:line. Do not start the next task.
If the work needs a path outside scope: STOP and ask the owner to amend the contract. Never widen scope silently.
